checks.finding: Core terms are concretely defined: required_facets/conditional_facets exact object shape (AC-037), review_check_ids shape (Field Definitions + AC-038, round-3 addition), the Gate implementation identity schema's scan-root/wrapper-grouping/symlink rules (REQ-003(c)/AC-016/AC-017), and delivery_strategy.kind's required-presence-but-open-vocabulary split (AC-004). No remaining term leaves two implementers free to build materially different behavior.

Cross-checked Goals/Non-goals/Field Definitions/AC set against investigation.md's Open Questions: minimum_enforcement's optionality (AC-005) and delivery_strategy's required-presence (AC-004) are consistently distinguished; OQ-002/OQ-003 rulings match REQ-001's schema description (no top-level conditions field; open, non-empty delivery_strategy.kind); REQ-003(a) gates[].id uniqueness and REQ-003(i)/AC-039 capabilities[].id uniqueness (round-3 addition) are stated as independently checked, non-masking constraints with no conflicting language found anywhere in the reviewed set.

REQ-004 states the registry_digest generator's fragment-selection input is '--capability-ids ..., --gate-ids ..., or both (at least one required, or --whole ...)' -- i.e. invoking the script with none of --capability-ids/--gate-ids/--whole is an explicitly stated failure mode. AC-024/TEST-024 (acceptance-tests.md) cover dedupe, stable ID sort, and unknown-ID hard failure, but no AC or TEST row names the expected diagnostic/exit behavior when no selector flag is supplied at all, nor a fixture combining --capability-ids and --gate-ids together (the explicitly permitted 'or both' case). Downstream failure mode: an implementer authoring the Planned test suite has no acceptance-tests.md row instructing them to write this fixture, so one implementer could silently default the no-flag invocation to --whole while another raises an error -- both consistent with the current AC set, producing observably divergent CLI behavior for the identical invocation. This belongs to spec review, not design/task review, because the gap is between a rule stated in requirements.md (REQ-004's 'at least one required') and acceptance-tests.md's row-by-row test coverage for that same requirement -- no later-phase artifact is positioned to catch it. Major (not Critical) because it is a missing observable acceptance criterion for a stated constraint rather than a contradictory goal or a safety/workflow boundary; not Minor because it is a concrete implementer-choice divergence risk on an already-normative rule, not a mere clarification.

OQ-001 (upgrade_reasons vocabulary) and OQ-004 (unregistered-script detection mechanism) are explicitly marked open pending a human/Epic A6 decision (investigation.md Open Questions; Roles and Permissions names the human maintainer as resolver). OQ-002/OQ-003 are marked RESOLVED by orchestrator ruling with the resolution reflected consistently in REQ-001/AC-004/AC-006. The Epic A1 canonicalizer/schema dependency is explicitly flagged as blocking REQ-004's implementation task and driving a recorded drift-check obligation on the DSL field allowlist (Dependencies section; investigation.md INV-004a), not silently assumed.

Approval/governance boundaries are in scope here (Spec-Review-Status/Impl-Review-Status must remain human-set; protected-file edits must go through human-copy) so SKIP does not apply. AC-029 gives a concrete, three-part testable verification procedure (staged candidate + MANIFEST.sha256 under human-copy/, byte-identical live guard-invariants.json until a human applies it, post-cp path verification in the regenerated file), and Roles and Permissions explicitly assigns who may flip Status fields and who resolves OQ-001/OQ-004, giving a testable boundary rather than an implicit or unstated one.

Aside from the EDGE-CASE-COVERAGE gap noted above (an untested-but-already-stated behavior, not an undefined one), every REQ-001..006 has matching Field Definitions entries and AC/TEST rows in acceptance-tests.md, and the round-1/round-2 findings (minimum_enforcement contradiction, facet entry-shape ambiguity, review_check_ids shape ambiguity, capabilities[].id uniqueness gap) all read as closed with concrete, schema-testable language in this round's artifacts. Design.md-level architecture choices (exact DSL JSON node envelope, provider-terms.json file format) are appropriately left open per the calibration's False-Positive Guard and do not force the design reviewer to invent missing product behavior.
